# SUPPURATIVE THROMBOPHLEBITIS

Obtain blood cultures before starting empirical antimicrobials. Peripheral vein suppurative thrombophlebitis may require surgical intervention in addition to antimicrobial therapy. The usual treatment for jugular vein suppurative thrombophlebitis (Lemierre's syndrome) and vena cava suppurative thrombophlebitis is prolonged antimicrobial therapy, with or without radiological or thrombolytic clot removal. Consult Infectious Diseases and Vascular Surgery for more information. Modify antimicrobial regimen and narrow coverage based on results of culture and susceptibility tests.

# Duration of therapy

A minimum of 4 to 6 weeks of antimicrobial therapy is appropriate and may be abbreviated in peripheral vein infections based on patient specific factors. Antimicrobial therapy should be continued until there is definite clinical response and oral antimicrobial therapy may be used after completion of initial course of intravenous therapy.

Therapy:
## Empirical treatment for peripheral vein infections and central vein infections associated with a venous catheter

Preferred:

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] <AND> ceftriaxone 1 gm IV q24h ($) [M]

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R <AND> gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h ($)

[R,O]

## Empirical treatment for jugular vein infection (also known as Lemierre's) or suppurative pelvic vein infection

Consultation with Surgery and Infectious Diseases is encouraged.

Preferred:

Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h ($$) R

Alternative:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h ($) DI

## For catheter-associated infection, add vancomycin to one of the above treatment regimens

< ADD > Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R
